name: Harvest Finance
loss_note: about $33.8M lost by the vaults, about $24M kept by the attacker, about $2.5M sent back
tldr: The vaults priced their shares using a Curve pool that a flash loan could nudge. Buy shares cheap, push the price back, sell them dear, repeat.
what: Harvest Finance was a yield farming protocol. Users deposited stablecoins like USDC and USDT into vaults, which put the money to work in Curve's Y pool.
happened: In about seven minutes, the attacker used flash loans to swing stablecoin prices inside the Curve pool, deposited into the vaults at a skewed share price and withdrew at a better one. Each round made a small profit; around 30 rounds added up to millions.
bug: The vault valued its shares from a live pool price that one large trade could move. Its built-in check only reacted to big price swings, so moves of about 1% passed silently.
prevent: Never value deposits and withdrawals from a price that can be moved inside one transaction. Use time-weighted prices, tighter checks, or block deposit and withdraw in the same transaction.
lesson: If one trade can move your price, a flash loan can move it a lot, for free, as many times as it likes.

sources.title: Harvest Finance Releases Attack Postmortem After Losing $24 Million (BeInCrypto)
